record.paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
record.original_question: How does QCD make the transition from the high-parton-density saturation regime, where small-x gluons form a weakly coupled nonlinear many-body system, to the confinement regime of QCD?

evidence.quote: The emergence of this non-linear regime, called parton saturation, in which QCD stays weakly coupled, is a fundamental consequence of QCD dynamics.

There are more fundamental questions, still unexplored, in the field of QCD at high parton density. How does the transition from the saturation regime to confinement happen? Does the QCD coupling run with Qs? Are classical fields still the right degrees of freedom? What are the universality properties of the saturation regime? p+A and e+A collisions offer special opportunities to explore this many-body system of strongly-correlated gluons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the gauge theory of strong interactions based on the non-abelian gauge group SU(3) with quark and gluon fields, consider hadronic scattering at very high energies. In the high-energy (small Bjorken-x) limit, the gluon density inside a hadron grows rapidly with decreasing x, and non-linear gluon recombination effects become important when occupation numbers reach order 1/α_s, defining a dynamically generated saturation scale Q_s(x). In this saturation regime the system behaves as a weakly coupled (since α_s(Q_s) ≪ 1 when Q_s is large) but highly non-linear many-body system of gluons, often described by classical color fields (e.g. the Color Glass Condensate effective theory and the JIMWLK / BK evolution equations). At low momentum scales, by contrast, QCD is in its confinement regime, where color is confined, the coupling is strong, and the relevant degrees of freedom are color-singlet hadrons.

Provide a quantitative, first-principles description of the transition between these two regimes. Specifically:

(a) Determine, within QCD, the mechanism by which the description in terms of weakly coupled, classical, high-occupancy small-x gluon fields with characteristic scale Q_s evolves, as Q_s is decreased toward Λ_QCD, into the confining regime characterized by hadronic (color-singlet) degrees of freedom.

(b) Decide whether the QCD coupling effectively runs with the saturation scale Q_s in this transition, and identify the correct effective degrees of freedom (classical color fields vs. hadronic / non-perturbative modes) on each side of and within the transition region.

(c) Establish the universality properties of the saturation regime, i.e. determine to what extent observables in the saturation regime depend only on Q_s (and possibly a small set of further parameters) and are independent of the specific hadronic target, and characterize how such universality is modified or lost as one approaches confinement.
artifact.status_search_result: The transition from the small-x gluon saturation regime (Color Glass Condensate) to the confinement regime of QCD is widely regarded as an outstanding open problem in high-energy QCD. Recent reviews on saturation physics, the Electron-Ion Collider science case, and CGC literature continue to list this as an unsolved fundamental question, motivating experimental programs at the EIC and in p+A / e+A collisions.

status_evidence.title: Science Requirements and Detector Concepts for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC Yellow Report)
status_evidence.snippet: Understanding the transition from the dilute partonic regime to the dense, saturated regime, and ultimately to confinement, remains a central open question that the EIC aims to address.
status_evidence.claim: Major recent community reports describe the saturation-to-confinement transition as an open question.

status_evidence.title: The Color Glass Condensate and small-x physics (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The matching of the CGC effective theory to the non-perturbative, confining regime of QCD at scales of order Λ_QCD is not under theoretical control.
status_evidence.claim: Standard CGC reviews state that the matching to confinement is not yet understood.
